title: Sections balancing and its strict completion square
statement: Fix a finite-field datum $D$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne D.p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbb Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Put $R=\mathcal O_E$, $s=\operatorname{Spec}(D.k)$, and let $B$ be the completed integral coefficient sheaf on the pro-etale site of $s$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $S$ be integral point tensor data and let $c$ be its canonical model witness [def-sf-point-fibre-tensor-models]. Let $C,J$ be flat-term K-flat $B$-module complexes [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined], write $\Gamma$ for termwise final-object sections, let $P$ be any $R$-module cochain complex, and let $\eta:P\to\Gamma C$ be any chain map. Suppose $\rho$ is any strict tower isomorphism with the local multiplication formula of [lem-pod-point-balanced-quotient-tower]. Then there is a chain map $\beta:P\otimes\Gamma J\to\Gamma\operatorname{Tot}(C\otimes J)$ with the generator rule $x\otimes h\mapsto\eta(x)\otimes h$. Use sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], signed total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], and the strict Roos functor $H=\operatorname{Cone}(1-t)[-1]$ on termwise products [def-weil-strict-roos-model]. If $u$ is the specified identity scalar-extension completion augmentation [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison], then $\beta\,\Gamma(u\,H(\rho)^{-1})=(\eta\otimes1)c(C,J)$ as chain maps. No quasi-isomorphism or normalization of $\eta$ is assumed.

proof.text: Take the section-tensor comparison on each bidegree, totalize and precompose with eta tensor identity. The signed differentials give a chain map beta with the displayed generator rule. Project its composite with the completion augmentation onto every quotient-product coordinate. The balancing formula and the unit quotient formula give exactly the first coordinate of the canonical tensor completion. The shifted coordinate is zero on both sides by the unit formula and canonical.second. Sections preserve products and biproducts; the two cone projections, all product projections, and the tensor total injections jointly detect equality, proving the chain equation.

theorem point_sections_balancing_completion
    (hl : l ≠ D.p) (S : PointIntegralTensorData D l hl E)
    (canonical : PointIntegralTensorCanonical D l hl E S)
    (P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1, u} (Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l
      E))) ℤ)
    (C J : (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E (Spec (.of D.k))).FullSubcategory)
    (rho : (integralOperationsTensorTowerFunctor l E (Spec (.of D.k))).obj
      (C.obj, J.obj) ≅ (integralScalarTowerFunctor l E E (AlgHom.id ℚ_[l] E) (Spec (.of D.k))).obj
      ((PointDerivedHom.total.{u, u} D.k (completedIntegralCommRingSheafUnrestricted l E (Spec (.of
      D.k)))) C.obj J.obj))
    (hbal : PointQuotientTowerBalanced D l E C.obj J.obj rho)
    (eta : P ⟶ (pointIntegralComplexSections D l E).obj C.obj) :
    ∃ beta : P ⊗ (pointIntegralComplexSections D l E).obj J.obj ⟶ (pointIntegralComplexSections D l
      E).obj ((PointDerivedHom.total.{u, u} D.k (completedIntegralCommRingSheafUnrestricted l E
      (Spec (.of D.k)))) C.obj J.obj),
      PointSectionsBalancingProperty D l E hl S canonical P C J rho eta beta
lean.note: The named predicates have exactly the displayed generator and strict completion formulas as their real bodies, with no holes. The sections completion equation is also used by the parent normalization predicate, which is definitionally the same equation. No data definition is chosen from the existence theorem.
